summary: SSE final frame dropped after upstream HTTP/2 graceful shutdown behind CDN
description: Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports that SSE streams occasionally finish without the final paragraph — the streamer closes without the terminal "event: end" chunk. Impact: customers see truncated outputs for long streaming responses (~4-12s generation) ~1-2% of sessions during weekday peak. Environment: prod, routed via CDN (FastEdge) -> Redwood edge-proxy (http2 upstream to runtime) -> serving-runtime. Observed behavior: final JSON chunk with choice 'finish_reason' is missing; client receives connection close without terminal delimiter. Expected behavior: final chunk and terminal event should be delivered before stream close.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ParcelFlow dedicated account in us-east to start an SSE generation with redwood-7B-instruct, prompt ~200 tokens expected finalization at 6-10s
2) Route traffic through customer CDN (FastEdge) configured with http2 fronting Redwood edge in us-east
3) Observe stream with client that logs SSE frames and final 'event: end' marker
4) Intermittent: connection closes from upstream during finalization and last chunk never arrives

edge-proxy 2026-03-09T18:22:42Z WARN sse: dropping tail fragment due to write error: write tcp 10.2.4.8:443->10.4.1.22:52314: use of closed network connection

comments: 2026-03-09 19:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported 0.8% of streams truncated during peak window 18:00-19:00 UTC. Attached client logs and sample request id=svc-1294.

2026-03-09 20:12 - Alex Thompson (SRE): Initial triage suggests upstream HTTP/2 GOAWAY coincides with last-token write. Added edge-proxy logs and bumped to Sev1. Linking internal INT-882 where similar pattern observed in synthetic tests.

2026-03-10 09:30 - Dev (edge-proxy): Reproduced in staging by inducing graceful shutdown (nghttpd GOAWAY). Observed that buffered SSE fragments are not flushed when server issues GOAWAY then closes connection quickly. PR referenced for fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4312

2026-03-12 15:00 - Alex Thompson (SRE): Deployed hotfix to edge-proxy to delay connection close until write buffers drained. Monitoring for regression. Customer notified of workaround (see resolution).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: HTTP/2 GOAWAY from upstream CDN causes edge-proxy to transition connection state; if the edge-proxy does not flush pending SSE frames before closing underlying TCP, the last frame is lost.
Confirmed by reproducer: synthetic script that sends a 3-chunk SSE stream, then triggers upstream GOAWAY immediately after final chunk is queued -> final chunk missing at client.
Edge-proxy codepath uses non-blocking writes; when GOAWAY observed it initiated connection close callback that cancels outstanding write completion in some code paths.
Serving-runtime observed no internal generation error; generation completed and final tokens were produced and queued to downstream.
Related to prior ticket SUP-981024 (terminal output lost after short TLS stall) but root cause here is HTTP/2 graceful shutdown ordering rather than TLS stall.
Affected surface area: SSE over HTTP/2 and websockets proxied via edge-proxy when upstream initiates GOAWAY/stream reset close during tail-write.
resolution: Workaround (customer-facing): Configure CDN to increase the GOAWAY drain timeout on upstream connections (FastEdge setting: upstream_grace_period to 5s) OR enable retry-on-close in client to re-request with 'last_event_id' semantics (ParcelFlow implemented quick client-retry for truncated responses).

Fix deployed: edge-proxy hotfix delays final TCP close until write buffer drain completion and treats GOAWAY as 'drain and close' instead of immediate close. Hotfix rolled to us-east edge nodes 2026-03-12 14:45 UTC.

Follow-ups: add unit/integration test for SSE flush on upstream GOAWAY, add dashboard alert for upper-percentile truncated_stream_rate, and update streaming runbook with 'http2-goaway' troubleshooting steps. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4312
Status: monitoring — initial metric shows truncated stream rate dropped from 0.8% to 0.03% in canary. Awaiting 48h observation window before closure.
